notes_for_us: A combat training dummy has no option row. npc-population is explicitly not this - the file says a market crowd is not a spawner and the reverse holds too - and Shooter's target-practice is a firing range. So the one placed object this prompt actually asks for ships as free text with no route.

Nearly the whole prompt is animation scripting, and mechanics absorbed it correctly. But the last two sentences carry the entire layout job and arrive as an afterthought - step 0's triage handles this well, and it is worth knowing the layout content can be 3% of the text.

'Do not use basic blocks. Generate high-quality textures' is a material constraint over the whole build with nowhere to live. It is not theme, not an option and not mechanics, and it is the kind of instruction a user will judge the result by.

notes_for_us: The shape had to carry two things at once. world-underground is the only row that expresses a building over a basement, but it is written for mining layers, so a dealership with a garage under it takes a shape whose description is about surface and subterranean strata. It routes correctly and reads wrongly.

Simulation's shape list is about where the player's plot is, and this prompt's defining feature is a single fixed building. plot-shared, plot-isolated and world-open all miss for the same reason, and the substitution rule was the only way through.

The prompt names three buildings and no ground between them. Everything about the open world - how big, what else is in it, whether there is traffic - came from the word 'monde ouvert', which is doing more work here than any other word in the prompt.
